newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle feeders poised to trade - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle feeders poised to trade - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet early Wednesday, but expected to trade later in the day, according to feedlot sources.
Early bids at $65.00 per cwt were passed by owners pricing cattle mostly at $67.00, with a few at $68.00, sources said. Sales were expected at $66.00, steady with last week, some sources said.
Prices were seen underpinned by light supplies of finished cattle.
"If bids come to $66.00, we'll move a lot of cattle," said one feedlot manager in western Kansas.
Cattle owners would be willing sellers at $66.00 because they would still make a marginal profit of $20 to $30 per head at that level, one feedlot operator said.
Supplies of finished cattle remain tight as feedlots continue to stay very current in their marketings.
Lower beef prices Tuesday could keep a lid on fed cattle prices but beef movement was relatively strong at the lower prices, some sources noted.
Beef prices were quoted down $0.31 to $0.60 per cwt on 241 fabricated loads sold, according to USDA.
